title: Cherry blossom motif
subtitle: A five-petal blossom with picot edges in pale pink, 7 cm
excerpt: The cherry blossom works five rounded petals with a picot scallop along the outer edge of each, giving a delicate fringed look at 7 cm in 4-ply cotton. The picot edge catches light differently from the smooth violet petal and gives a lace-like quality. Used as a hair accessory backing, shawl scatter motif, and spring garland element.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Crochet, Volume 6 (1891), spring blossom and picot flower chapter (Internet Archive). Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopedia of Needlework (1886), crochet picot flower section.
heroPrompt: A crochet cherry blossom motif in pale pink 4-ply cotton with five rounded petals and picot scallop edges, 7 cm across, photographed flat on a white background in soft daylight.

chartDefinition.title: Cherry blossom motif
chartDefinition.caption: 10dc magic ring. Five petals: ch-7 arch, dc-htr-htr-picot-htr-htr-dc fill. Pink French knot stamens at centre.

glossaryTerms.definition: Three chains closed back into the first chain with a slip stitch. Adds a small decorative loop at the petal tip.

content.text: The cherry blossom builds five petals from a 10-dc magic ring, each petal a ch-7 arch filled with dc and htr stitches around a
picot

at the outer tip. The picot sits at the petal apex and creates the scalloped silhouette that distinguishes this from a plain five-petal motif. Five evenly spaced petals fill the ring completely. Pink French knot stamens at the centre complete the botanical look.

attrs.title: Materials for one motif
attrs.body: About 3 g of pale pink 4-ply cotton. A 2.5 mm hook. Tapestry needle. Deep pink embroidery thread for stamens. Scissors.

content.text: Gauge
Each finished cherry blossom motif measures 7 cm across in 4-ply cotton with a 2.5 mm hook.
Stitches used
chain (ch), slip stitch (sl st), magic ring (MR) — UK and US shared.
double crochet (dc) — UK; US "single crochet".
half treble (htr) — UK; US "half double crochet".
picot (p) — ch 3, sl st in first ch.
Pattern
Centre ring
Form a magic ring. Ch 1. 10dc into ring. Sl st to first dc to join. (10 dc.)
Petals — 5 times

Work 5 petals, one into each dc of the ring then sl-st the next dc as spacer: *Ch 7. Into the ch-7 arch work: Dc. Htr. Htr. Picot (ch 3, sl st in first ch). Htr. Htr. Dc. Sl st into the ring dc you started from. Sl st into the next dc (spacer).* Repeat from * to * four more times. Fasten off.

definition.title: Cherry blossom motif
definition.caption: 10dc magic ring. Five petals: ch-7 arch with dc/htr/htr/picot/htr/htr/dc. Picot at petal tip.

content.text: Finishing
Embroider 3 to 5 French knot stamens at the very centre using deep pink thread. Weave in ends. Pin the petals open and allow to dry flat.
Care
Handwash in cool water. The picot tips hold without stiffening. Lay flat to dry.
What to try next

The intricate snowflake (crochet-snowflake-intricate) uses the same picot construction at a larger scale. The violet (crochet-flower-violet) is the same construction without picots for a simpler five-petal companion.
